04-01.title: Otto von Bismarck
04-01.description: The "Iron Chancellor" who unified the German states into a single empire in 1871 through a calculated blend of war, diplomacy, and realpolitik.

04-01.title: Debbie Reynolds
04-01.description: Hollywood legend who charmed audiences as Kathy Selden in Singin' in the Rain and sustained a dazzling career across seven decades of film and stage.

04-01.title: William Harvey
04-01.description: English physician who revolutionized medicine by demonstrating that blood circulates continuously through the body pumped by the heart.

04-01.title: TIROS-1 Launches
04-01.description: NASA's Television Infrared Observation Satellite beamed back the very first television picture taken from space, transforming weather forecasting forever.

04-01.title: Netherlands Legalizes Same-Sex Marriage
04-01.description: The Netherlands became the first country in the world to grant full marriage rights to same-sex couples, a landmark moment for LGBTQ+ equality.

04-01.title: Ladies of the Canyon — Joni Mitchell
04-01.description: Joni Mitchell's sun-dappled third album introduced "Big Yellow Taxi" and "Woodstock" to the world, cementing her as the poet laureate of the counterculture.

04-01.title: Grease
04-01.description: John Travolta and Olivia Newton-John set hearts racing in this era-defining musical that became one of the highest-grossing films of the decade.

04-02.title: Marvin Gaye
04-02.description: The "Prince of Soul" crafted some of Motown's most sensual and politically charged music, from "Sexual Healing" to the groundbreaking concept album What's Going On.

04-02.title: Charlemagne
04-02.description: King of the Franks who united much of Western Europe under his reign and was crowned the first Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Leo III on Christmas Day 800.

04-02.title: Walter Chrysler
04-02.description: American automobile manufacturer who founded the Chrysler Corporation in 1925, building it into one of the "Big Three" US automakers.

04-02.title: Beethoven's First Symphony Premieres
04-02.description: Ludwig van Beethoven personally conducted the premiere of his Symphony No. 1 in C major in Vienna, announcing himself as the heir to Haydn and Mozart.

04-02.title: Ponce de León Reaches Florida
04-02.description: Spanish explorer Juan Ponce de León came ashore near present-day St. Augustine, becoming the first European documented to land on the North American mainland's east coast.

04-02.title: "Let's Get It On" — Marvin Gaye
04-02.description: Marvin Gaye's silky masterpiece of sensual yearning became one of the most celebrated soul recordings ever made, topped the US charts for two weeks.

04-02.title: Titanic
04-02.description: James Cameron's sweeping romantic epic about the doomed ocean liner became the first film in history to gross over $1 billion at the worldwide box office.

04-03.title: Marlon Brando
04-03.description: Revolutionary American actor whose raw, Method-driven performances in A Streetcar Named Desire and The Godfather permanently changed the art of screen acting.

04-03.title: Eddie Murphy
04-03.description: Comedian and actor who became the biggest box-office draw of the 1980s through Saturday Night Live, Beverly Hills Cop, and an electrifying stand-up persona.

04-03.title: Doris Day
04-03.description: America's sweetheart of the silver screen who starred opposite Hollywood's biggest leading men and recorded enduring hits like "Que Sera, Sera."

04-03.title: Pony Express Begins
04-03.description: The first Pony Express rider galloped out of St. Joseph, Missouri, inaugurating a relay mail system that could deliver a letter to Sacramento in just ten days.

04-03.title: Jesse James Killed
04-03.description: Notorious outlaw Jesse James was shot in the back of the head by Robert Ford at his home in St. Joseph, Missouri, ending a career of bank and train robberies.

04-03.title: Martin Luther King Jr.'s Mountaintop Speech
04-03.description: On the eve of his assassination, Dr. King delivered his prophetic "I've Been to the Mountaintop" speech in Memphis, rallying striking sanitation workers.

04-03.title: Planet of the Apes
04-03.description: Charlton Heston crash-lands on a world ruled by intelligent apes in this chilling sci-fi allegory whose shocking twist ending remains one of cinema's most iconic moments.

04-04.title: Maya Angelou
04-04.description: Poet, memoirist, and civil rights activist whose autobiographical I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings became a landmark of American literature.

04-04.title: Robert Downey Jr.
04-04.description: Actor who staged one of Hollywood's greatest comebacks to embody Tony Stark across the Marvel Cinematic Universe, anchoring a billion-dollar franchise.

04-04.title: Muddy Waters
04-04.description: The "Father of Modern Chicago Blues" electrified Delta blues traditions and directly inspired the Rolling Stones, Led Zeppelin, and a generation of rock musicians.

04-04.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Assassinated
04-04.description: Civil rights leader Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. was shot and killed by James Earl Ray on the balcony of the Lorraine Motel in Memphis, Tennessee.

04-04.title: NATO Founded
04-04.description: Twelve nations signed the North Atlantic Treaty in Washington, D.C., creating a collective defense alliance that would define Western security for generations.

04-04.title: "Respect" — Aretha Franklin
04-04.description: Aretha Franklin transformed Otis Redding's song into an anthem of female empowerment and civil rights, topping the charts and winning her two Grammy Awards.

04-04.title: Psycho
04-04.description: Alfred Hitchcock's terrifying masterpiece invented the modern horror film with Anthony Perkins as Norman Bates and the unforgettable shower scene that changed cinema.

04-05.title: Bette Davis
04-05.description: Two-time Oscar winner whose ferocious talent and fierce independence made her Hollywood's most formidable actress across five decades of films.

04-05.title: Booker T. Washington
04-05.description: Educator and orator who rose from slavery to found Tuskegee Institute and became the most influential African American leader of his era.

04-05.title: Agnetha Fältskog
04-05.description: Swedish singer whose crystalline soprano voice powered ABBA to international superstardom, making them one of the best-selling music acts in history.

04-05.title: First Presidential Veto
04-05.description: George Washington issued the very first presidential veto in American history, rejecting a congressional apportionment bill on constitutional grounds.

04-05.title: Bosnian War Begins
04-05.description: Bosnian Serb snipers opened fire on peaceful anti-war demonstrators in Sarajevo, killing two protesters and marking the bloody opening of the Bosnian War.

04-05.title: Tracy Chapman — Tracy Chapman
04-05.description: Tracy Chapman's self-titled debut introduced her acoustic folk-soul sound to a generation, with "Fast Car" and "Talkin' 'bout a Revolution" earning her three Grammy Awards.

04-05.title: American Beauty
04-05.description: Sam Mendes' searing suburban satire starring Kevin Spacey swept the Academy Awards, winning five Oscars including Best Picture and Best Director.

04-06.title: Merle Haggard
04-06.description: Country music legend from Bakersfield whose hard-lived honky-tonk songs about working-class life and prison earned him a spot among the genre's all-time greats.

04-06.title: James Watson
04-06.description: Molecular biologist who co-discovered the double-helix structure of DNA with Francis Crick in 1953, earning a Nobel Prize and transforming biology forever.

04-06.title: Paul Rudd
04-06.description: Actor and comedian whose everyman charm anchored roles in Clueless and the Ant-Man Marvel films while earning him the title of People's Sexiest Man Alive.

04-06.title: United States Enters World War I
04-06.description: Congress declared war on Germany, bringing America into the Great War after years of neutrality and ultimately tipping the balance toward Allied victory.

04-06.title: First Modern Olympics Open
04-06.description: The first modern Olympic Games opened in Athens, Greece, reviving an ancient tradition and launching the world's greatest sporting spectacle.

04-06.title: Invasion of Privacy — Cardi B
04-06.description: Cardi B's debut album debuted at number one and became the first solo female rap album to win the Grammy for Best Rap Album, breaking chart records along the way.

04-06.title: The Greatest Show on Earth
04-06.description: Cecil B. DeMille's spectacular big-top extravaganza won Best Picture at the Academy Awards, despite its reputation as one of the most surprising Oscar champions ever.

04-07.title: Francis Ford Coppola
04-07.description: Director of The Godfather trilogy and Apocalypse Now, Coppola reshaped Hollywood in the 1970s and remains one of American cinema's supreme visionaries.

04-07.title: Billie Holiday
04-07.description: Jazz vocalist of devastating emotional depth whose phrasing was unlike anyone before or since, and whose rendition of "Strange Fruit" became a civil rights touchstone.

04-07.title: Jackie Chan
04-07.description: Hong Kong action superstar who combined martial arts with breathtaking stunts and physical comedy to create a genre all his own across more than 150 films.

04-07.title: "South Pacific" Broadway Premiere
04-07.description: Rodgers and Hammerstein's beloved musical South Pacific opened on Broadway to rapturous reviews and became one of the longest-running shows of its era.

04-07.title: World Health Day Established
04-07.description: The World Health Organization inaugurated the first World Health Day, observed annually on April 7 to raise global awareness about public health issues.

04-07.title: Nick of Time — Bonnie Raitt
04-07.description: Bonnie Raitt's comeback album swept the 1990 Grammys, winning Album of the Year and transforming her overnight from cult favorite to mainstream star.

04-07.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
04-07.description: Stanley Kubrick's enigmatic science-fiction epic premiered in Washington, D.C. and changed cinema with its breathtaking visuals, philosophical depth, and the menacing HAL 9000.

04-08.title: Mary Pickford
04-08.description: "America's Sweetheart" who became Hollywood's first global superstar, co-founded United Artists, and helped establish the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.

04-08.title: Jacques Brel
04-08.description: Belgian chanson master whose emotionally shattering songs — "Ne Me Quitte Pas," "Amsterdam" — established him as one of the most influential European songwriters of the 20th century.

04-08.title: Vivienne Westwood
04-08.description: Visionary British fashion designer who weaponized punk aesthetics to challenge mainstream taste and reshaped the language of fashion from the King's Road outward.

04-08.title: Venus de Milo Discovered
04-08.description: A farmer on the Greek island of Milos unearthed the ancient marble statue later known as the Venus de Milo, now displayed as one of the Louvre's most treasured works.

04-08.title: Apple's iTunes Store Opens
04-08.description: Apple launched the iTunes Music Store, selling songs for 99 cents each and moving one million tracks in its first week — reshaping the music industry forever.

04-08.title: Toys in the Attic — Aerosmith
04-08.description: Aerosmith's career-defining third album with "Sweet Emotion" and "Walk This Way" became their best-selling record in America with nine million copies sold.

04-08.title: Falling into You — Céline Dion
04-08.description: Céline Dion's blockbuster album soared to number one around the world and became one of the best-selling records of the 1990s on the strength of its power ballads.

04-09.title: Dennis Quaid
04-09.description: Versatile American actor who brought gritty authenticity to roles in The Right Stuff, The Big Easy, and Far from Heaven across a career spanning four decades.

04-09.title: Carl Perkins
04-09.description: Pioneering rockabilly guitarist who wrote "Blue Suede Shoes" — the first record ever to top the pop, country, and R&B charts simultaneously.

04-09.title: Marc Jacobs
04-09.description: American fashion designer who helmed Louis Vuitton for sixteen years and built his eponymous label into one of the most celebrated names in contemporary fashion.

04-09.title: Lee Surrenders at Appomattox
04-09.description: Confederate General Robert E. Lee surrendered to Ulysses S. Grant at Appomattox Court House, effectively ending the American Civil War after four years of bloodshed.

04-09.title: First Public Library in America
04-09.description: The Peterborough Town Library in New Hampshire opened as the first tax-supported public library in the United States, establishing a democratic model for free access to books.

04-09.title: "Blue Suede Shoes" — Carl Perkins
04-09.description: Carl Perkins' rockabilly anthem became the first record to simultaneously hit number one on the pop, country, and R&B charts, making it one of rock and roll's founding texts.

04-09.title: Never Been Kissed
04-09.description: Drew Barrymore shines as a copy editor who goes undercover at a high school in this charming romantic comedy that became a sleeper hit of the late 1990s.

04-10.title: Joseph Pulitzer
04-10.description: Hungarian-American newspaper titan who transformed American journalism with his New York World and endowed the Pulitzer Prizes that bear his name.

04-10.title: Omar Sharif
04-10.description: Egyptian actor of magnetic charisma who captivated audiences as Sherif Ali in Lawrence of Arabia and the title role of Doctor Zhivago, earning two Golden Globe wins.

04-10.title: Q-Tip
04-10.description: Rapper and producer and creative engine of A Tribe Called Quest, whose jazz-infused alternative hip-hop on The Low End Theory reshaped rap's sonic palette.

04-10.title: Paul McCartney Announces Beatles Breakup
04-10.description: Paul McCartney issued a press release announcing he had quit the Beatles, officially ending the greatest band in rock history after a decade of revolutionary music.

04-10.title: First Image of a Black Hole Unveiled
04-10.description: Scientists from the Event Horizon Telescope project released humanity's first photograph of a black hole — the supermassive colossus at the heart of galaxy M87.

04-10.title: "Whole Lotta Shakin' Goin' On" — Jerry Lee Lewis
04-10.description: Jerry Lee Lewis released his debut charting single, a ferocious piano-pounding performance that announced one of rock and roll's most untameable talents.

04-10.title: House of Wax
04-10.description: Vincent Price terrorizes New York in this groundbreaking color 3-D horror film, which opened to massive crowds and launched a new era in immersive cinema.

04-11.title: Joss Stone
04-11.description: Devon-born soul prodigy who burst onto the charts at sixteen with a voice decades beyond her years and released the critically praised debut The Soul Sessions.

04-11.title: Joel Grey
04-11.description: Tony and Oscar-winning American actor whose sinister, androgynous Emcee in Cabaret became one of the most indelible performances in musical theatre history.

04-11.title: Meshell Ndegeocello
04-11.description: Groundbreaking bassist, singer, and songwriter who blended funk, soul, jazz, and hip-hop into a singular voice that influenced a generation of musicians.

04-11.title: Bob Dylan's Live Debut
04-11.description: A twenty-year-old Bob Dylan made his New York City live debut opening for blues legend John Lee Hooker at Gerde's Folk City in Greenwich Village.

04-11.title: USS Holland Purchased
04-11.description: The US Navy purchased its first submarine, the USS Holland, ushering in a new era of undersea warfare that would reshape naval strategy in the 20th century.

04-11.title: Beatles Place 14 Songs on Billboard Hot 100
04-11.description: The Beatles simultaneously occupied 14 spots on the Billboard Hot 100 — a record that has never been matched — with "Can't Buy Me Love" at number one.

04-11.title: Singin' in the Rain
04-11.description: Gene Kelly, Donald O'Connor, and Debbie Reynolds danced and sang their way through Hollywood's transition to talkies in what many consider the greatest musical film ever made.

04-12.title: David Letterman
04-12.description: Late-night television pioneer who revolutionized talk show comedy across seventeen years at NBC and twenty-two at CBS, influencing every host who followed.

04-12.title: Josephine Baker
04-12.description: American-born French entertainer, civil rights activist, and French Resistance spy whose dazzling performances in 1920s Paris made her the first Black international superstar.

04-12.title: Beverly Cleary
04-12.description: Beloved children's author whose irrepressible character Ramona Quimby appeared in nine books and introduced millions of young readers to the pleasure of fiction.

04-12.title: Yuri Gagarin Orbits the Earth
04-12.description: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space, completing a 108-minute orbit of the Earth in Vostok 1 and transforming the Space Race.

04-12.title: Space Shuttle Columbia First Launch
04-12.description: NASA launched the first Space Shuttle, Columbia, inaugurating an era of reusable crewed spacecraft that would serve the agency for thirty years.

04-12.title: "What's Going On" — Marvin Gaye
04-12.description: Marvin Gaye's profound protest single against the Vietnam War and police brutality became a Motown landmark and the catalyst for his landmark concept album.

04-12.title: Grease 2
04-12.description: The sequel to the beloved original brought Maxwell Caulfield and Michelle Pfeiffer to the halls of Rydell High in this energetic if commercially disappointing follow-up.

04-13.title: Thomas Jefferson
04-13.description: Primary author of the Declaration of Independence, third President of the United States, and Renaissance polymath who shaped the philosophical foundations of American democracy.

04-13.title: Samuel Beckett
04-13.description: Nobel Prize-winning Irish playwright whose Waiting for Godot stripped drama to its existential essentials and defined the Theatre of the Absurd for generations.

04-13.title: Garry Kasparov
04-13.description: Russian chess prodigy who became World Chess Champion at 22 and held the title for fifteen years, later becoming an outspoken democracy advocate.

04-13.title: Handel's Messiah Premieres
04-13.description: George Frideric Handel's magnificent oratorio Messiah had its world premiere in Dublin to a sold-out crowd, with Handel himself conducting the performance.

04-13.title: Apollo 13 Oxygen Tank Explodes
04-13.description: An oxygen tank aboard Apollo 13 exploded 200,000 miles from Earth, transforming a lunar landing mission into one of history's most dramatic survival stories.

04-13.title: Sticky Fingers — The Rolling Stones
04-13.description: The Rolling Stones' Andy Warhol-designed album — with its actual working zipper — unleashed "Brown Sugar" and "Wild Horses" on an astonished world.

04-13.title: Avengers: Infinity War
04-13.description: Thanos snapped half the universe out of existence in Marvel's most ambitious crossover event, bringing together dozens of heroes in a film of staggering scale.

04-14.title: Loretta Lynn
04-14.description: Country music's Coal Miner's Daughter who wrote and recorded frank, feminist anthems decades ahead of her time and became one of the genre's most revered figures.

04-14.title: Peter Capaldi
04-14.description: Scottish actor and Oscar-winning director who embodied the sardonic Malcolm Tucker in The Thick of It before taking on the mantle of the Twelfth Doctor in Doctor Who.

04-14.title: Anthony Michael Hall
04-14.description: Quintessential 1980s teen film actor who defined the nerdy outsider in John Hughes classics including Sixteen Candles, The Breakfast Club, and Weird Science.

04-14.title: Abraham Lincoln Shot
04-14.description: President Abraham Lincoln was shot by John Wilkes Booth at Ford's Theatre in Washington, D.C. while watching Our American Cousin; he died the following morning.

04-14.title: RMS Titanic Strikes Iceberg
04-14.description: At 11:40 PM, the RMS Titanic struck an iceberg in the North Atlantic on her maiden voyage — within three hours the "unsinkable" liner had vanished beneath the waves.

04-14.title: "Coal Miner's Daughter" — Loretta Lynn
04-14.description: Loretta Lynn's autobiographical signature song told the story of her Appalachian upbringing with earthy pride and became a country music standard.

04-14.title: The Breakfast Club
04-14.description: John Hughes locked five archetypical teenagers in detention for a Saturday in this incisive coming-of-age drama that became the defining film of an entire generation.

04-15.title: Leonardo da Vinci
04-15.description: The ultimate Renaissance man: painter of the Mona Lisa and The Last Supper, engineer, anatomist, and inventor whose notebooks brimmed with designs centuries ahead of their time.

04-15.title: Emma Watson
04-15.description: British actress who grew up before the world's eyes as Hermione Granger in the Harry Potter series and emerged as a prominent feminist and UN Women Goodwill Ambassador.

04-15.title: Chris Stapleton
04-15.description: Kentucky country singer-songwriter whose soulful voice and literary songwriting on his Grammy-sweeping debut Traveller established him as the genre's most respected voice.

04-15.title: RMS Titanic Sinks
04-15.description: The RMS Titanic sank in the North Atlantic at 2:20 AM, claiming the lives of more than 1,500 people in one of the deadliest peacetime maritime disasters in history.

04-15.title: Jackie Robinson Breaks Color Barrier
04-15.description: Jackie Robinson took the field for the Brooklyn Dodgers, becoming the first African American to play in Major League Baseball and changing American sports forever.

04-15.title: "The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face" — Roberta Flack
04-15.description: Roberta Flack's hypnotic rendition of Ewan MacColl's folk ballad reached number one and stayed atop the US charts for six weeks, winning the Grammy for Record of the Year.

04-15.title: Titanic
04-15.description: Germany's dramatic black-and-white telling of the Titanic disaster was one of the most expensive German films ever produced at the time of its wartime release.

04-16.title: Charlie Chaplin
04-16.description: The "Tramp" who made the world laugh and weep — Chaplin's silent comedies from The Kid to Modern Times transformed cinema into a universal language of humanity.

04-16.title: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar
04-16.description: Six-time NBA champion and all-time leading scorer whose unstoppable skyhook made him the most dominant center in basketball history.

04-16.title: Selena Quintanilla-Pérez
04-16.description: The "Queen of Tejano Music" who was crossing over to mainstream pop stardom when she was tragically killed at twenty-three, leaving a legacy that only grew with time.

04-16.title: Giovanni da Verrazzano Discovers New York Harbor
04-16.description: Italian explorer Giovanni da Verrazzano, sailing for France, became the first European to enter New York Harbor and the Hudson River estuary.

04-16.title: Ellis Island Record Day
04-16.description: Ellis Island processed a record 11,747 immigrants in a single day, a peak moment of the mass European immigration that transformed American society.

04-16.title: The Rolling Stones — The Rolling Stones
04-16.description: The Rolling Stones' self-titled debut album crashed into the UK charts at number one, introducing a raw, blues-drenched alternative to the Beatles' pop charm.

04-16.title: The Kid
04-16.description: Charlie Chaplin's first feature-length film paired his iconic Tramp with the six-year-old Jackie Coogan in a comedy-drama of genuine emotional power.

04-17.title: J. P. Morgan
04-17.description: American financier who dominated Wall Street at the turn of the 20th century, bankrolling railroads and steel companies while shaping the modern American economy.

04-17.title: Victoria Beckham
04-17.description: British pop icon who sang as Posh Spice with the Spice Girls before reinventing herself as one of the most respected names in European fashion design.

04-17.title: William Holden
04-17.description: Hollywood golden age star who won an Academy Award for Stalag 17 and delivered iconic performances in Sunset Boulevard and The Bridge on the River Kwai.

04-17.title: Bay of Pigs Invasion
04-17.description: CIA-trained Cuban exiles landed at the Bay of Pigs attempting to overthrow Fidel Castro, but the disastrous operation collapsed within days in a humiliation for the Kennedy administration.

04-17.title: Apollo 13 Crew Returns Safely
04-17.description: Astronauts Jim Lovell, Jack Swigert, and Fred Haise splashed down safely in the Pacific Ocean after guiding their crippled spacecraft home from the Moon.

04-17.title: Doolittle — Pixies
04-17.description: The Pixies' genre-defining second album with "Here Comes Your Man" and "Debaser" invented the quiet-loud dynamic that Nirvana's Kurt Cobain called his primary influence.

04-17.title: Schindler's List
04-17.description: Steven Spielberg's devastating Holocaust masterpiece, shot in stark black and white, won seven Academy Awards including Best Picture and Best Director.

04-18.title: Conan O'Brien
04-18.description: Harvard-educated comedian and television host who revolutionized late-night TV with his surreal wit on Late Night, The Tonight Show, and his own TBS program Conan.

04-18.title: David Tennant
04-18.description: Scottish actor beloved as the Tenth Doctor in Doctor Who whose brooding charisma also powered acclaimed runs in Broadchurch and the stage productions of the Royal Shakespeare Company.

04-18.title: Rick Moranis
04-18.description: Canadian comedy legend who brought irresistible nerdish charm to Ghostbusters, Spaceballs, and Honey I Shrunk the Kids before stepping back from Hollywood to raise his children.

04-18.title: San Francisco Earthquake and Fire
04-18.description: A catastrophic 7.9-magnitude earthquake struck San Francisco at dawn, and the fires that followed destroyed 25,000 buildings and killed over 3,000 people.

04-18.title: Paul Revere's Midnight Ride
04-18.description: Paul Revere and William Dawes set out from Boston to alert colonial militias that British troops were marching to seize rebel arms at Concord, Massachusetts.

04-18.title: "What's Love Got to Do with It" — Tina Turner
04-18.description: Tina Turner's ice-cool comeback single hit number one on the Billboard Hot 100, won three Grammy Awards, and announced her triumphant return as a solo superstar.

04-18.title: Aladdin
04-18.description: Disney's musical Arabian Nights adventure starring a charming street thief and a wisecracking Robin Williams Genie became one of the studio's highest-grossing animated films.

04-19.title: Kate Hudson
04-19.description: American actress who won a Golden Globe for her breakout performance as Penny Lane in Almost Famous and established herself as one of Hollywood's most bankable stars.

04-19.title: Hayden Christensen
04-19.description: Canadian actor who brought brooding intensity to the role of Anakin Skywalker in the Star Wars prequel trilogy, becoming one of the saga's most pivotal figures.

04-19.title: Levon Helm
04-19.description: Drummer and vocalist for The Band whose earthy Arkansas voice and powerhouse drumming drove classics like "The Weight" and "The Night They Drove Old Dixie Down."

04-19.title: Battles of Lexington and Concord
04-19.description: "The shot heard round the world" was fired at Lexington Green, Massachusetts, as colonial militiamen clashed with British Regulars in the opening battles of the American Revolution.

04-19.title: Mars Helicopter Achieves First Flight
04-19.description: NASA's Ingenuity helicopter became the first powered aircraft to achieve controlled flight on another planet, hovering above the surface of Mars for 39.1 seconds.

04-19.title: "The Weight" — The Band
04-19.description: Levon Helm and The Band's rustic masterpiece, drawn from the debut album Music from Big Pink, blended Americana, gospel, and rock into something entirely new.

04-19.title: My Big Fat Greek Wedding
04-19.description: Nia Vardalos wrote and starred in this sleeper comedy about a Greek-American family navigating a cross-cultural romance that grossed over $368 million on a $5 million budget.

04-20.title: Luther Vandross
04-20.description: Velvet-voiced R&B singer and producer whose romantic ballads — "A House Is Not a Home," "Here and Now" — earned him eight Grammy Awards and sold over 35 million records.

04-20.title: Joan Miró
04-20.description: Spanish Surrealist painter whose playful, dreamlike canvases of biomorphic shapes and bold primary colors were a uniquely joyful contribution to modern art.

04-20.title: Andy Serkis
04-20.description: British actor who pioneered motion-capture performance as Gollum in The Lord of the Rings and Caesar in Rise of the Planet of the Apes, creating a new form of screen acting.

04-20.title: Deepwater Horizon Explosion
04-20.description: The Deepwater Horizon oil rig exploded in the Gulf of Mexico, killing eleven workers and triggering the largest marine oil spill in US history over the following 87 days.

04-20.title: Freddie Mercury Tribute Concert
04-20.description: A star-studded concert at Wembley Stadium celebrated the life of Queen frontman Freddie Mercury with Elton John, David Bowie, and George Michael performing to 72,000 fans.

04-20.title: "Never Too Much" — Luther Vandross
04-20.description: Luther Vandross launched his solo career with this irresistible debut single, showcasing the silken tenor voice that would make him the reigning prince of quiet storm R&B.

04-20.title: Avengers: Endgame
04-20.description: The culmination of twenty-two Marvel films premiered at the Los Angeles Convention Center, going on to briefly become the highest-grossing film of all time.

04-21.title: Queen Elizabeth II
04-21.description: Britain's longest-reigning monarch who served for seventy years with unwavering dignity, becoming a global symbol of continuity, duty, and the Commonwealth.

04-21.title: Iggy Pop
04-21.description: The "Godfather of Punk" whose incendiary performances with The Stooges and solo work like "Lust for Life" made him one of rock's most electrifying and influential figures.

04-21.title: James McAvoy
04-21.description: Scottish actor of remarkable range who inhabited Professor X in the X-Men films and earned widespread acclaim for stage performances with the Royal Shakespeare Company.

04-21.title: "Heartbreak Hotel" Reaches Number One
04-21.description: Elvis Presley's first RCA single, a dark, echoing lament of loneliness, topped the Billboard charts and launched the King of Rock and Roll into global superstardom.

04-21.title: Prince Dies
04-21.description: Musical genius Prince Rogers Nelson was found unresponsive at his Paisley Park complex in Minnesota at age 57, prompting an outpouring of grief from fans worldwide.

04-21.title: "Lust for Life" — Iggy Pop
04-21.description: Written with David Bowie during their legendary Berlin period, this thunderous Iggy Pop anthem endures as one of rock's most visceral and indestructible opening riffs.

04-21.title: The Passion of Joan of Arc
04-21.description: Carl Theodor Dreyer's silent masterpiece captured the trial and martyrdom of Joan of Arc through radical close-ups that remain among cinema's most harrowing images.

04-22.title: Jack Nicholson
04-22.description: Three-time Oscar winner whose volcanic charisma in Chinatown, One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest, and As Good as It Gets made him Hollywood's most celebrated leading man.

04-22.title: Vladimir Lenin
04-22.description: Russian revolutionary leader who led the Bolshevik seizure of power in 1917, founded the Soviet Union, and reshaped the political landscape of the 20th century.

04-22.title: Glen Campbell
04-22.description: Virtuoso guitarist and country-pop crossover king whose Wichita Lineman and Rhinestone Cowboy earned him Grammy Awards and cemented a uniquely gentle brand of American stardom.

04-22.title: First Earth Day
04-22.description: Twenty million Americans took to the streets in the first Earth Day, a grassroots environmental protest that led directly to the creation of the EPA and the Clean Air Act.

04-22.title: Land Run of 1889
04-22.description: The Oklahoma Land Rush opened two million acres of the Unassigned Lands to settlers; at noon a pistol shot started a stampede of 50,000 would-be homesteaders.

04-22.title: "Like a Prayer" — Madonna
04-22.description: Madonna's genre-defying single blended gospel and pop in a video so controversial it cost her a Pepsi endorsement deal, yet the song topped charts in multiple countries.

04-22.title: Tommy
04-22.description: Ken Russell's psychedelic rock opera adapted The Who's landmark concept album with a cast including Tina Turner, Elton John, and Roger Daltrey as the deaf, dumb, and blind pinball wizard.

04-23.title: William Shakespeare
04-23.description: The greatest writer in the English language, whose 37 plays and 154 sonnets plumbed the full range of human experience with unmatched psychological depth and poetic power.

04-23.title: Roy Orbison
04-23.description: Texan singer-songwriter whose operatic tenor and heartrending ballads of lost love — "Crying," "In Dreams," "Oh, Pretty Woman" — made him one of rock's most distinctive voices.

04-23.title: Max Planck
04-23.description: German physicist whose quantum hypothesis — that energy is emitted in discrete packets called quanta — launched the quantum revolution that underpins all modern physics.

04-23.title: Shakespeare's Probable Birth and Death Day
04-23.description: William Shakespeare died on April 23, 1616 — traditionally also his birthday — making this date a unique convergence of birth and death for the world's most celebrated writer.

04-23.title: Ramones Debut Album Released
04-23.description: The Ramones unleashed their 29-minute, 14-track debut album, compressing rock and roll to its most explosive, no-frills essence and igniting the punk revolution.

04-23.title: Sticky Fingers — The Rolling Stones
04-23.description: Released with Andy Warhol's iconic zipper cover, this album's "Brown Sugar" and "Wild Horses" marked the peak of the Rolling Stones' creative powers.

04-23.title: The Public Enemy
04-23.description: James Cagney's electrifying performance as a ruthless Chicago gangster made him a star overnight in this Warner Bros. crime classic that defined the gangster film genre.

04-24.title: Barbra Streisand
04-24.description: Singer, actress, and director who conquered Broadway, Hollywood, and pop charts to become one of the best-selling music artists of all time with two Oscars and eight Grammys.

04-24.title: Shirley MacLaine
04-24.description: Oscar-winning actress whose decades-long career produced iconic performances in The Apartment, Terms of Endearment, and Steel Magnolias alongside an outspoken personal philosophy.

04-24.title: Sachin Tendulkar
04-24.description: Regarded as cricket's greatest ever batsman, the "Little Master" from Mumbai scored 100 international centuries and played at the highest level for an extraordinary 24 years.

04-24.title: Easter Rising Begins
04-24.description: Irish republicans seized key buildings in Dublin and proclaimed the Irish Republic, launching an armed rebellion against British rule that ultimately led to Irish independence.

04-24.title: Library of Congress Established
04-24.description: The Library of Congress was founded in Washington, D.C. with an initial appropriation of $5,000, growing into the world's largest library with over 170 million items.

04-24.title: "People" — Barbra Streisand
04-24.description: Barbra Streisand's signature ballad from Funny Girl topped the charts and became the anthem of her career, showcasing the soaring power of her extraordinary voice.

04-24.title: Superman
04-24.description: Richard Donner's landmark production made audiences believe a man could fly, with Christopher Reeve's performance setting the standard for all superhero films to come.

04-25.title: Al Pacino
04-25.description: Method-trained actor whose blazing intensity in The Godfather, Scarface, and Dog Day Afternoon made him the defining film star of a remarkable era in American cinema.

04-25.title: Ella Fitzgerald
04-25.description: The "First Lady of Song" whose flawless pitch, three-octave range, and virtuosic scat singing established her as the greatest jazz vocalist of the 20th century.

04-25.title: Renée Zellweger
04-25.description: Two-time Academy Award-winning actress who embodied Bridget Jones, channeled Judy Garland in Judy, and brought fierce vulnerability to her roles in Cold Mountain and Chicago.

04-25.title: Hubble Space Telescope Deployed
04-25.description: NASA's Space Shuttle Discovery deployed the Hubble Space Telescope, which despite initial mirror problems went on to capture the deepest images of the universe ever taken.

04-25.title: First Bell Solar Cell Demonstrated
04-25.description: Bell Telephone Laboratories publicly demonstrated the first practical silicon solar cell, generating enough electricity from sunlight to power a small toy Ferris wheel.

04-25.title: "A-Tisket, A-Tasket" — Ella Fitzgerald
04-25.description: Ella Fitzgerald's charming swing version of the nursery rhyme became her first major hit, staying at number one for seventeen weeks and launching her solo career.

04-25.title: Scarface
04-25.description: Brian De Palma's operatic crime epic with Al Pacino as Cuban immigrant Tony Montana became one of the most quoted and imitated films in pop culture history.

04-26.title: Ma Rainey
04-26.description: The "Mother of the Blues" whose raw, powerful voice and commanding stage presence made her the first great professional blues singer and an inspiration for Bessie Smith.

04-26.title: Carol Burnett
04-26.description: Comedy legend whose groundbreaking variety program The Carol Burnett Show ran for eleven seasons, making her one of the first women to produce and star in her own TV series.

04-26.title: Channing Tatum
04-26.description: American actor, producer, and dancer who parlayed his background in male revue shows into the blockbuster Magic Mike franchise and a string of crowd-pleasing action comedies.

04-26.title: Bombing of Guernica
04-26.description: Nazi Germany's Condor Legion bombed the Basque town of Guernica in support of Franco's forces, killing hundreds of civilians in an atrocity Pablo Picasso immortalized on canvas.

04-26.title: Studio 54 Opens
04-26.description: New York's legendary Studio 54 nightclub opened its doors, becoming the epicenter of the disco era and an exclusive playground for celebrities, artists, and the beautiful people.

04-26.title: Throwing Copper — Live
04-26.description: Live's third album, with anthemic singles "Lightning Crashes" and "I Alone," sold over eight million copies in America and became one of the defining albums of the mid-1990s.

04-26.title: Guernica
04-26.description: Alain Resnais' short documentary film juxtaposed Picasso's iconic anti-war painting against images from the Spanish Civil War in a haunting meditation on destruction and memory.

04-27.title: Ulysses S. Grant
04-27.description: Union general who led the North to victory in the Civil War and served two terms as President, becoming a symbol of both American military triumph and Reconstruction-era struggle.

04-27.title: Samuel Morse
04-27.description: American painter turned inventor who co-developed the electric telegraph and the dot-dash code that bears his name, shrinking the communications of a continent to seconds.

04-27.title: Ace Frehley
04-27.description: Lead guitarist of KISS who created the fire-spitting, rocket-launching persona of the Spaceman and whose blazing solos helped power the band to arena-rock superstardom.

04-27.title: Magellan Killed in the Philippines
04-27.description: Portuguese explorer Ferdinand Magellan was killed in battle at Mactan Island, Philippines by local chief Lapulapu, during the first circumnavigation of the globe.

04-27.title: South Africa's First Democratic Election
04-27.description: South Africa held its first fully democratic election open to all races, with Nelson Mandela's ANC winning in a landslide that ended the apartheid era.

04-27.title: "Rock and Roll All Nite" — KISS
04-27.description: KISS released their career-defining anthem on the Dressed to Kill album, a fist-pumping celebration of the rock lifestyle that became one of the most recognizable hard rock songs ever.

04-27.title: Avengers: Age of Ultron
04-27.description: Marvel's second Avengers ensemble film pitted Earth's mightiest heroes against the AI villain Ultron in a globe-trotting spectacle that grossed $1.4 billion worldwide.

04-28.title: Harper Lee
04-28.description: American novelist whose debut and only major novel To Kill a Mockingbird, published in 1960, won the Pulitzer Prize and became one of the most beloved books in American literature.

04-28.title: Penélope Cruz
04-28.description: Spanish actress and the first Spaniard to win an Academy Award, acclaimed for Volver, Vicky Cristina Barcelona, and her decades-long collaboration with director Pedro Almodóvar.

04-28.title: James Monroe
04-28.description: The fifth President of the United States whose "Era of Good Feelings" administration issued the Monroe Doctrine, establishing American hemispheric influence for generations.

04-28.title: Mutiny on the Bounty
04-28.description: Fletcher Christian led a mutiny against Captain William Bligh aboard HMS Bounty in the South Pacific, setting Bligh and 18 loyalists adrift in an open boat.

04-28.title: Mussolini Executed
04-28.description: Italian dictator Benito Mussolini was captured and shot by communist partisans near Lake Como, and his body was hung upside down in Milan's Piazzale Loreto.

04-28.title: Chicago Transit Authority — Chicago
04-28.description: Chicago's sprawling brass-rock debut double album introduced a bold fusion of jazz, rock, and pop that earned the band a Grammy nomination for Best New Artist.

04-28.title: Bridesmaids
04-28.description: Kristen Wiig's semi-autobiographical comedy about female friendship, rivalry, and romantic chaos smashed box-office expectations and redefined the Hollywood comedy landscape.

04-29.title: Daniel Day-Lewis
04-29.description: The only male actor to win three Academy Awards for Best Actor, Day-Lewis brought total physical and psychological immersion to roles in My Left Foot, There Will Be Blood, and Lincoln.

04-29.title: Uma Thurman
04-29.description: American actress whose fearless performances in Pulp Fiction and the Kill Bill saga established her as one of contemporary cinema's most hypnotic and distinctive screen presences.

04-29.title: Jerry Seinfeld
04-29.description: Stand-up comedian who co-created and starred in Seinfeld, the sitcom that ran for nine seasons as the most watched show in America and changed the face of television comedy.

04-29.title: Hair Opens on Broadway
04-29.description: The American Tribal Love-Rock Musical Hair opened on Broadway, celebrating the counterculture with nudity, rock music, and an anti-Vietnam War message that shocked and thrilled audiences.

04-29.title: Los Angeles Riots Begin
04-29.description: Six days of civil unrest erupted in Los Angeles after the acquittal of four LAPD officers in the Rodney King beating case, resulting in 63 deaths and $1 billion in damage.

04-29.title: "Aquarius / Let the Sunshine In" — The 5th Dimension
04-29.description: Drawn from the Hair musical, this medley spent six weeks at number one and became a defining anthem of the late 1960s Age of Aquarius counterculture movement.

04-29.title: Fast Five
04-29.description: The fifth entry in the Fast & Furious franchise reinvented the series as an action-heist epic by bringing in Dwayne Johnson and setting the whole thing loose in Rio de Janeiro.

04-30.title: Kirsten Dunst
04-30.description: American actress who transitioned seamlessly from child prodigy in Interview with the Vampire to blockbuster star in the Spider-Man trilogy and indie darlings like Melancholia.

04-30.title: Gal Gadot
04-30.description: Israeli actress and model who became a global icon playing Wonder Woman, bringing warmth, strength, and gravitas to the DC Extended Universe's most beloved character.

04-30.title: Willie Nelson
04-30.description: Outlaw country legend whose braided pigtails, battered guitar Trigger, and laid-back Texas drawl made him one of American music's most enduring and beloved figures.

04-30.title: George Washington Inaugurated
04-30.description: George Washington was sworn in as the first President of the United States at Federal Hall in New York City, inaugurating the American democratic republic.

04-30.title: Fall of Saigon
04-30.description: North Vietnamese forces captured Saigon, ending the Vietnam War as the last US personnel were evacuated by helicopter from the roof of the American embassy.

04-30.title: Aftermath — The Rolling Stones
04-30.description: The Rolling Stones' first album composed entirely of original Jagger-Richards material topped the UK charts and showcased a new ambition and range in the band's songwriting.

04-30.title: Iron Man
04-30.description: Robert Downey Jr. suited up as Tony Stark in this international release that launched the Marvel Cinematic Universe and sparked the superhero movie boom of the 21st century.
